title: Dundee Neutrophil Isolation Protocol from Whole Blood
author: Ying Fan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bnhtmb6n
materials: Immediately snap freeze samples in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Collect blood sample
steps.instruction: Collect exactly 10 mL of whole blood into a BD Vacutainer tube; do not discontinue collection prematurely and mix gently by inverting the tube 7–8 times.

steps.title: Transfer blood to Falcon tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the 10 mL of blood into a 50 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Add first EDTA solution
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of “EDTA Stock Solution 1” (0.1 M EDTA‑PBS) to the blood and mix gently.

steps.title: Add isolation cocktail
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL of the isolation cocktail solution from the neutrophil isolation kit to the blood sample.

steps.title: Resuspend magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Vortex the RapidSpheres magnetic beads (from the neutrophil isolation kit) for 30 seconds to fully resuspend the fine beads.

steps.title: Add magnetic beads to blood
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL of the resuspended RapidSpheres magnetic beads to the blood sample.

steps.title: Incubate first binding
steps.instruction: Mix the blood sample gently by inverting the tube and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Top up with second EDTA
steps.instruction: Top the tube up to the 50 mL mark with “EDTA Stock Solution 2” (1 mM EDTA‑PBS).

steps.title: Gentle pipette mixing
steps.instruction: Mix by gently pipetting up and down 2–3 times.

steps.title: First magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the tube into the magnetic separator, remove the lid, and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Collect first enriched suspension
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette the enriched cell suspension (containing neutrophils) into a new 50 mL Falcon tube, avoiding contact with the tube side that was against the magnet and leaving approximately 10 mL of red‑blood‑cell suspension at the bottom.

steps.title: Add beads for second binding
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL RapidSpheres magnetic beads to the tube obtained in the previous step.

steps.title: Incubate second binding
steps.instruction: Mix gently by inverting the tube and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Second magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the tube into the magnet, remove the lid, and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Collect second enriched suspension
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette the enriched cell suspension into a new 50 mL Falcon tube, avoiding contact with the magnet side and leaving approximately 5 mL of suspension at the bottom.

steps.title: Remove residual beads
steps.instruction: Place the tube from the previous step into the magnet, remove the lid, and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes to ensure complete removal of magnetic beads.

steps.title: Collect pure neutrophils
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette the neutrophil suspension into a new 50 mL Falcon tube, avoiding the magnet side and leaving approximately 5 mL of suspension at the bottom.

steps.title: Record neutrophil volume
steps.instruction: Note that the neutrophil suspension volume at this stage is 30–35 mL.

steps.title: Adjust final volume with EDTA
steps.instruction: Top up the isolated cells with EDTA Stock Solution 2 (1 mM) to a final volume of approximately 41 mL, pipette up and down to mix, then divide equally into two tubes (~20 mL each).

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge both tubes at 335 × g for 5 minutes at °C (temperature not specified) using a Beckman Coulter Allegra X‑15R centrifuge; set acceleration and deceleration to 5 (maximum is 10).

steps.title: Prepare MLi‑2 stock
steps.instruction: During the centrifugation, retrieve the MLi‑2 inhibitor stock (200 µM, 1000×) from the –80 °C freezer and let it equilibrate at room temperature for later use (steps 26 and 28).

steps.title: Discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Immediately after centrifugation, carefully discard the supernatant without disturbing the neutrophil pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend pellets in RPMI
steps.instruction: Resuspend each cell pellet in 10 mL RPMI medium at room temperature by gently pipetting up and down 4 times.

steps.title: Label treatment tubes
steps.instruction: Label one tube “DMSO” and the other “MLi‑2”.

steps.title: Add DMSO to control
steps.instruction: To the “DMSO” tube, add 10 µL DMSO and mix gently by pipetting up and down 2 times with a 10 mL pipette.

steps.title: Add MLi‑2 to treatment
steps.instruction: To the “MLi‑2” tube, add 10 µL 200 µM MLi‑2 stock (final concentration 200 nM) and mix gently by pipetting up and down 2 times with a 10 mL pipette.

steps.title: Incubate with inhibitors
steps.instruction: Incubate both tubes for 30 minutes at room temperature, mixing gently by inversion every 10 minutes.

steps.title: Retrieve DIFP stock
steps.instruction: Remove 0.5 M DIFP stock from the –80 °C freezer and place it in a fume hood on ice.

steps.title: Retrieve microcystin‑LR stock
steps.instruction: Remove 1 mg/mL Microcystin‑LR stock from the –80 °C freezer and let it thaw at room temperature.

steps.title: Defrost lysis buffer aliquot
steps.instruction: Defrost a 0.25 mL aliquot of the lysis buffer by allowing it to sit at room temperature, then place it on ice for later use (step 34).

steps.title: Prepare DMSO resuspension buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 mL RPMI medium containing 1 µL DMSO and label this solution “DMSO Resuspension Buffer”.

steps.title: Prepare MLi‑2 resuspension buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 mL RPMI medium containing 1 µL 200 µM MLi‑2 and label this solution “MLi‑2 Resuspension Buffer”.

steps.title: Second centrifugation after incubation
steps.instruction: After the 30‑minute incubation, centrifuge both tubes at 335 × g for 5 minutes at °C (temperature not specified) with acceleration and deceleration set to 5 on the Beckman Coulter Allegra X‑15R.

steps.title: Discard supernatant post‑incubation
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant from each tube without disturbing the neutrophil pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend pellets in treatment buffers
steps.instruction: For the DMSO‑labeled sample, gently resuspend the pellet in 1 mL DMSO Resuspension Buffer and transfer to an Eppendorf tube labeled “DMSO”. For the MLi‑2‑labeled sample, gently resuspend the pellet in 1 mL MLi‑2 Resuspension Buffer and transfer to an Eppendorf tube labeled “MLi‑2”.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend DMSO pellet in 1 mL DMSO buffer and transfer.
Resuspend MLi‑2 pellet in 1 mL MLi‑2 buffer and transfer.

steps.title: Low‑speed centrifugation of resuspended cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge both Eppendorf tubes at 300 × g for 3 minutes at °C (temperature not specified).

steps.title: Prepare lysis buffer with inhibitors
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, add 0.25 µL 0.5 M DIFP and 0.25 µL 1 mg/mL Microcystin‑LR to 0.25 mL lysis buffer, mix, and keep on ice. Note: DIFP must be added to the lysis buffer within 15 minutes of cell lysis because it is unstable in aqueous solution.

steps.title: Return DIFP stock to freezer
steps.instruction: Return the remaining 0.5 M DIFP stock to the –80 °C freezer.

steps.title: Remove supernatant after low‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Immediately after the centrifugation in step 33, carefully remove all supernatant with a pipette without disturbing the neutrophil pellets.

steps.title: Place pellets on ice
steps.instruction: Place the tubes containing the neutrophil cell pellets on ice.

steps.title: Lyse DMSO‑treated cells
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL lysis buffer containing DIFP to the “DMSO” tube, then resuspend the pellet by pipetting up and down 5–10 times with a 100–200 µL pipette until all cells are lysed.

steps.title: Lyse MLi‑2‑treated cells
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL lysis buffer containing DIFP to the “MLi‑2” tube, then resuspend the pellet by pipetting up and down 5–10 times with a 100–200 µL pipette until all cells are lysed.

steps.title: Incubate lysates on ice
steps.instruction: Incubate the cell lysates on ice for 10 minutes.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation of lysates
steps.instruction: Place the “DMSO” and “MLi‑2” tubes into a centrifuge and spin at 14 000 rpm, 4 °C, for 15 minutes to pellet cell debris.

steps.title: Collect cleared lysates
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatants (containing neutrophil lysates) from each tube into new Eppendorf tubes and discard the debris pellets.

steps.title: Store lysate samples
steps.instruction: Store the collected lysate samples at –80 °C until further use or shipment on dry ice, keeping the samples frozen at all times.
